intro_html: Sweet and smoky is one of the oldest pairings in American barbecue, and here it happens in one bowl. A roasted sweet potato splits open, gets a pile of barbecue pulled pork dropped into it, then sour cream, onion and cilantro on top. No bun to buy, no bun to go stale, and the potato brings fiber and potassium that a white roll never did. This is also the easiest thing in the section to prep, because the two components store separately and reheat on their own schedules.
cost_closing_html: About $2.91 a bowl. The pork shoulder is nearly all of it. The sweet potato that holds the whole thing together is the cheapest item on the list.
shop_smart: Sweet potatoes are cheapest loose by the pound in fall. Look for ones that are even in thickness rather than the biggest in the bin, because they roast through at the same rate.
Buy a bone-in pork shoulder and slow cook it whole. It is the lowest cost per pound of protein in the meat case and the bone makes the juices better.
Barbecue sauce is worth making from pantry staples if you have them. If not, buy the store brand. One bottle covers this batch with plenty to spare.
Store the pork and the potatoes in separate containers. The potato reheats better on its own and does not go soggy under sauce all week. It costs nothing to split them.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Season the pork shoulder with salt, black pepper and smoked paprika, sear it in the vegetable oil, then slow cook it with the minced garlic, the diced onion and the bay leaves for 8 to 9 hours on low.
Scrub the sweet potatoes, prick them all over with a fork, and roast at 400F for about an hour until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Pull the pork apart with two forks and skim the fat off the cooking liquid.
Toss the shredded pork with the barbecue sauce and a few spoonfuls of the skimmed cooking liquid so it stays moist rather than pasty.
Split each roasted sweet potato lengthwise and press the flesh open with a fork to make room.
Fill each one with the barbecue pork and keep the sour cream, diced onion and chopped cilantro in separate containers to add at reheat.
portion_html: Set one roasted sweet potato in each of your 14 containers, then set your mixing pot of barbecue pork on the scale, subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1, divide by 14, and pile that exact weight into each potato. Every serving lands near 774 calories with 45 grams of protein.

head.description: Slow cooked barbecue pulled pork piled into roasted sweet potatoes with sour cream, onion and cilantro. A 14 serving no bun dinner built for meal prep.

steps: Season and sear the pork shoulder, then slow cook on low 8 to 9 hours with garlic and onion.
Roast the pricked sweet potatoes at 400F for about an hour.
Shred the pork and skim the fat off the cooking liquid.
Toss the pork with barbecue sauce and a little of the cooking liquid.
Split the sweet potatoes, fill with pork, and top with sour cream, onion and cilantro.
